result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.get_node_creation_order()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Get nodes in their creation order. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L4816-L4866){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.get_node_creation_order() ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Node creation order](/assets/graphs/get-node-creation-order.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="The shared four-node graph, added in the order A, B, C, D, with each node's id in an accent pill. The card returns the node ids from oldest to newest: 1, 2, 3, 4." width="100%"} Returns node IDs ordered by when they were added to the graph. The first node created appears first, the most recently created node appears last. Useful for temporal analysis or recreating graph construction history. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [list[int]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Node IDs in chronological creation order. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Node IDs already reflect creation order in most cases, but this method gives an explicit, guaranteed ordering to rely on: ::: {#d3e90c65 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph() graph.add_node(label="A") graph.add_node(label="B") graph.add_node(label="C") creation_order = graph.get_node_creation_order() creation_order ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` [1, 2, 3] ``` ::: ::: Mapping IDs back to labels confirms the nodes are listed in the order they were added: ::: {#6fa6b9c4 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} [graph.get_node(nid).label for nid in creation_order] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` ['A', 'B', 'C'] ``` ::: ::: This is handy for selecting, e.g., only the most recently created nodes: ::: {#2a626726 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ec.Graph().add_path_graph(10) recent = graph.get_node_creation_order()[-5:] graph.select_nodes_by_id(recent) graph.get_selected_node_ids() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` [9, 7, 10, 6, 8] ``` ::: :::
